Building the Project Team: Contractual Hiring and Compensation

Hello Morgan State University Faculty & Staff, In this module, we will review key post-award processes for Contractual Hiring and Personnel Compensation at Morgan State University. Topics include hiring contractual staff, hiring student research assistants, processing faculty summer research contracts, personnel cost tracking tips, and more. Please note that the processes detailed in this module are specific to grant-funded activities. Some of the information may also be relevant to state-funded actions; however, policy and procedural differences may apply. We strive to continuously review these lessons to provide up-to-date guidance on Morgan's sponsored project processes. For questions related to the activities covered in this module that are not addressed in the module content, please contact the ORA Training and Communications Coordinator: Mr. Ryan Mobley, CRA, CFRA, CPRA Email: ryan.mobley@morgan.edu Phone: 443-885-4771 Thank you, ORA Training Team

Self-paced ORA eTraining module. Source: https://share.articulate.com/P_TX_Sz334DiNOJZ0upJ7

## PSA: Before Drafting Contracts
Greetings MSU Faculty and Staff!
Before we jump into the exciting world of grant-funded compensation at MSU please review the important information below.
No Work Without Authorization
No one should be working for Morgan State University in any capacity without an authorized employment contract via the Office of Human Resources (OHR). This module will detail how to submit an employment contract for grant employees.
Review All Faculty Funding
Principal Investigators may often have funding available from multiple sources (various grants, summer teaching, etc.) that can contribute towards their maximum allowable summer salary (26.3% of their institutional base salary). These funding sources may have conflicting performance periods that may result in complicated contract planning. It is important for PIs, and their admins, to review the funding available to them and design contracts that meet the restrictions of each funding source.
Key Personnel Effort Changes
PIs, and their Key Personnel (typically Co-PIs), commonly have fixed effort/time commitments for their projects. Substantial deviation (more than 25%) from the effort commitment outlined in their project's Notice of Award will require sponsor approval.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Knowledge Check
Knowledge check: Test Your Current Knowledge A faculty member has multiple grants with a total summer salary available budget of $40,000. All of the project funding agencies allow the PI to claim up to 2.5 months salary. With a 9.5-month salary of $80,000, what is the maximum summer salary the PI could earn between their various projects?
  - $40,000  [incorrect]
  - $21,040 (26.3% of $80,000)  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  Note on "$40,000": Incorrect. Please try again.
  Note on "$21,040 (26.3% of $80,000)": Great job! A PI is only able to request up to 26.3% of their 9.5-month salary in summer funding between all funding sources. Even if more funding is available, they are unable to earn beyond this threshold.

## EPAFs: Requesting EPAF Access
Checking Your EPAF Access Status
All contract initiators must be granted access to submit EPAF contracts in Employee Self-Service. To check if you have EPAF access, go to the Employee Self-Service landing page and see if the "Electronic Personnel Action Forms (EPAF)" link is listed under My Activities.
Complete the content above before moving on.
Requesting EPAF Access in Workflow
Workflow: Requesting EPAF Access
A PI's supervisor or department/school budget officer should request EPAF access for the PI. A PI can request access for the staff on their project as needed.
Final Notes
Banner Links Homepage: Select Workflow
Submitting an EPAF access request is an action handled in Workflow. Please make your way to the Banner Links homepage here and select the Workflow icon. You will be prompted to enter your MSU credentials.
Select "My Processes"
On the left side of the screen you will see the "User Profile" taskbar under which is a link titled "My Processes."
Select "EPAF Access Request Form"
Select "EPAF Access Request Form" on the My Processes page. Please Note: If the link is unavailable, please contact the HR Information Systems team (HRIS@morgan.edu) for assisting in adding that workflow to your processes.
Enter Workflow Specifics
Here you must name the Workflow. A great example would be " Employee Name EPAF Access". Also, please list the employee's MSU email address. You can identify the priority as normal or urgent depending on how quickly the pin is needed. Now click the "Start Workflow" button.
Select Workflow
You may need to refresh your browser page a few times for the workflow to load on this page. Once loaded, select the correct workflow action.
Enter Employee Role and Submit
After selecting the "Initiator" role for those submitting contracts, please click the "Complete" button, and your workflow will be on its way! EPAF access is typically granted within 24-48 hours.
Extra: Add Missing Individuals to EPAF Approval Levels
Contract initiators may occasionally find that a PI, or their supervisor, may not be an available option to select for a particular EPAF approval queue level. In order to add a PI to the PI approval queue level please select "Approver" and the "12 PI Principal Investigator" approver type. Then, click the "Complete" button and your Workflow will be on the way!

## EPAFs: How to Submit a PIN Request
Submitting a PIN Request in Workflow
A Contractual PIN is among the first pieces of information you must collect before entering an EPAF for new position. Below, we detail exactly how to submit the request in Workflow.
How to Submit a Contractual PIN Request
Missing Workflow Access
If a pin is urgently needed, and the initiator does not have workflow access for pin requests, the same information required in the pin request can be emailed to OHR@morgan.edu to request a pin.
Banner Links Homepage: Select Workflow
Submitting a contractual pin request is an action handled in Workflow (a system utilized for a number of user-initiated access requests). Please make your way to the Banner Links homepage here and select the Workflow icon. You will be prompted to enter your MSU credentials.
Select "My Processes"
On the left side of the screen you will see the "User Profile" taskbar under which is a link titled "My Processes."
Select "Contractual PIN Request"
Select "Contractual PIN Request" on the My Processes page. Please Note: If the contractual pin request link is unavailable, contact the HR Information Systems team (hris@morgan.edu) for assistance in adding that workflow to your processes.
Enter Workflow Specifics
Here you must name the Workflow. A great example would be " Employee Name PIN Request." You can identify the priority as normal or urgent depending on how quickly the pin is needed. Now click the "Start Workflow" button.
Select Workflow
You may need to refresh your browser page a few times for the workflow to load. Once loaded, select the correct workflow action.
Enter Data and Submit
For each employee PIN request you will need to have the following information: Position Title Employment Type For faculty summer contracts the employment type would be full-time staff. For student contracts the select should always be "Student" regardless of the contract dates or hours worked. Budget Code (Project Budget Index) Supervisor Name and PIN The supervisor named is responsible for approving timesheets in Employee Self-Service. An initiator can enter "000000" in the Supervisor PIN box if they do not have it on hand. HR will review and update as needed. After entering all data please click the "Complete" button and your workflow will be on its way! Once the pin request has been successfully submitted the initiator will receive a pin to their email address typically within 24 hours.
Sharing PINs for Identical Positions
PINs may be shared by employees on a project so long as (a) the budget funding the contracts is the same and (b) the position title is the same. A contract initiator would simply use a new suffix for the subsequent contracts. For example, a PIN may be established for an Graduate Research Assistant (GRA) to work on Project XYZ (Index 123456). The PIN provided by OHR could be 647198-00. The first GRA would use 647198-00, the next 647198-01, and so on as needed.

## Electronic Personnel Action Forms (EPAF)
EPAFs: Steps Prior to Contract Entry
The process for hiring an employee will vary depending upon the individual. Please review the information below prior to entering any EPAF contract.
EPAF Access
All contract initiators must have EPAF access granted in Employee Self-Service. If you need access granted, please review the Workflow process in the "EPAFs: Requesting EPAF Access" lesson of this module.
Contractual PIN
In order to enter a contract in EPAF an initiator must have requested a contractual PIN through the Office of Human Resources. A detailed step-by-step tutorial on how to request a PIN can be found in the "EPAFs: How to Submit a PIN Request" lesson in this module.
EPAF Comments
Please review any comments included in your EPAF during the ORA approval process. ORA Budget Officers use the comments section to not required revisions or provide guidance needed for approval. If an EPAF appears to be pending longer than expected, check the comments section to ensure all requested updates have been addressed prior to contacting the ORA Budget Officers via email or phone for a status update.
LIGHT
Complete the content above before moving on.
EPAFs: Contracting for New and Returning Employees
EPAF Entry Process
After EPAF entry
After you have submitted your EPAF contract you must email a completed Position Description Form to OHR@morgan.edu . The email should reference the EPAF transaction ID# listed at the top of the EPAF page. Once the EPAF is approved by all parties, and a background check is completed, OHR will email the employee directly with a copy of their contract for signature.
Prior to EPAF Entry
All Contracts Have the position's contractual PIN ready. If you still need a PIN please review the request process in the "EPAFs: How to Submit a PIN Request" lesson of this module. Submit the Background Check Google Form to request a background check via HireRight. A contract will not be generated by OHR without a completed background check. Complete a Position Description Form (attached below). Maintain this for your records and provide to HR if requested. New Employees Only Submit a Employee ID Setup request. OHR will email the initiator within 24-48 hours with an MSU ID for the new employee. Student Employees Only Review student contract restrictions in the "Student Employees: Restrictions and Considerations" lesson of this module. Faculty Summer Contracts Review contract tips and calculation assistance in the "Faculty Summer Contracts" lesson in this module.
Banner Links Homepage: Employee Self-Service
To submit an EPAF you need to start at the Employee Self-Service Banner page. Please make your way to the Banner Links homepage here and select the "Employee Self-Service (Timesheet)" icon. You will be prompted to enter your MSU credentials.
My Activities: EPAF
Once the Employee Dashboard page has loaded you should see a taskbar on the right titled "My Activities." Click on the "Electronic Personnel Action Forms (EPAF)" link.
EPAF: Personnel Actions
On the "Personnel Actions" page an EPAF initiator will find two links: EPAF Originator Summary : Displays the EPAFs you have already submitted. New EPAF: Allows a user to initiate an EPAF. Please select the New EPAF option to begin the new contract entry process.
NEW EPAF Person Selection
On the New EPAF page you will need to complete the following: Identify the prospective employee. This can be done by entering the individual's first and last name, or MSU ID, and then click "Search". Select the employee record by clicking on their MSU ID. Note: It has been observed that occasionally students are not included in the employee database for EPAF entry. If you cannot query the student you wish to employ please email OHR@morgan.edu to add the student to the employee database. Enter the contract start date. On this page the "Query Date" should match the contract's start date. Assign the Approval Category. For grant-funded contracts this will typically be either (1) PF-10 Full Time Contract Staff or (2) PF-10 Part Time Contractual Staff. After entering all data click "Go."
Contractual PIN Entry
Enter the position's contractual PIN and suffix. The first contract utilizing a PIN will likely have the suffix "00" Employees on the same project can share the same 6-digit pin so long as they share the same position title as well. They would simply change the suffix. For example, a GRA may have a PIN (123456-00) and a second GRA on the same project may have the same Pin with a new suffix (123456-01)
Contract Specifics (Part 1)
Contract Type Primary: The employee's main contract. Secondary: Utilized for secondary contracts. Overload: Should be utilized for faculty summer contracts. Contract Number The "Contract Number" is the hourly rate for the contract. Annual Salary The "Annual Salary" is the total salary cost of the contract.
Contract Specifics (Part 2)
Contract Index/Fund The contract's accounting information (index, fund, org code, etc.) should auto populate based off of the information submitted in the PIN request. Please verify that the figures are accurate. Termination of Job: Jobs Effective Date The date entered in this section should reflect the stop date of the contract.
EPAF Routing Queue & Comments
The EPAF Routing Queue for grant-funded positions has been updated to allow for a more streamlined approval process and should be used for all grant-funded contracts. The image above details the default queue that should be strictly followed. Other individuals (Budget Officers, Directors, etc) can be added as FYI only. PI PI Supervisor (typically Chair or Dean) (Level 40): Graduate School Only necessary for graduate student EPAFs select Philip Inocencio (Level 60): Grant Accounting select Lucy Manyara (Level 89): HR Contractual Coordinator select Morenike Efese (Level 90): HR select Yolanda Elliott select "Apply" not "Approve" The "Comments" Section should have the following contract information: hours per week, grant title, grant performance period (current fiscal year), and PI name.
Submit the EPAF
After entering the EPAF Routing Queue an initiator should review their EPAF for accuracy. Then, click the "Save" button at the bottom left corner of the screen. If there aren't any errors you can click the "Submit" button at the bottom of the screen. Your EPAF is now officially on the way!

Contract Revisions and Continuations
PF-10 Revisions: A contract revision might be submitted to change a contract's hourly rate, total salary, or end date. ## Student Employees: Restrictions and Considerations
Student Contracts: What You Need to Know
Student employee contracts have additional considerations that PIs, and their support staff, must adhere to. Prior to entering a contract for a student, email OHR@morgan.edu to ensure the student is in employee database for EPAF entry.
Hour Restrictions
Student employees are allowed to work up to 20 hours per week during the academic year and 40 hours per week during the summer. This restriction is inclusive of ALL contracts the student may have at MSU. Doctoral students may work up to 40 hours per week year-round.
Can This Student Receive an employment contract?
There are situations where a student cannot be offered an employment contract with MSU. Such situations may include receiving Title III funding, receiving federal stipend support, the student's particular visa status, etc. Moreover, for inclusion in an employment contract, students are required to possess a social security number (SSN). Should a student lack one, the Principal Investigator (PI) is responsible for liaising with the Office of International Student & Faculty Services to facilitate communication with the Social Security Administration. The turnaround time for receiving a SSN is roughly 1-2 weeks so plan ahead. It is vital that PIs speak with prospective student employees before drafting any contracts to determine if there may be other activities that would disallow the employee from working on your project.
Suggested Hourly Rates
The minimum wage in Maryland as of Jan. 1, 2024 is $15 per hour. However, ORA has provided a suggested hourly rate range based on the student's status and experience. While these ranges are generally accepted, the chosen rate may vary by school and project complexity. Undergraduate: $15-20 per hour Graduate: $18-23 per hour Doctoral: $20-25 per hour Further information can be found in PI Handbook #3: Grant-Related Processes .

## Faculty Summer Contracts
Key Information: Division of Academic Affairs
Every spring the Division of Academic Affairs releases a memo which details the specific information necessary for drafting summer contracts. The pertinent information is identified below.
Contract Start/Stop Dates
All summer faculty contracts (grant contracts, summer teaching, etc.) should occur within the start and stop dates listed on the Academic Affairs memo.
Total Working Days
For Summer 2026, there are a total of 52 working days for faculty summer contracts. This excludes Memorial Day, Juneteenth, and Independence Day. This is because the contract term (less than 2.5 months), and the contract start dates, are not sufficient to qualify for claiming these holiday pay days.
Hourly Rate Calculations
For grant-funded contracts ORA requires faculty summer contract hourly rates to match the calculated maximum hourly rate using the formula in the AA memo. A simplified version of the AA memo formula for Summer 2026 is: [(9.5 month salary * .263)/416]
Maximum Summer Salary
The maximum amount a faculty member can earn across ALL summer contracts, including summer teaching, at MSU is limited to 26.3% of their academic contract (9.5 or 12-month).

Additional Faculty Summer Contract Information
https://articulateusercontent.com/assets/rise/assets/block-defaults/paraglide_thumb.jpg
Cover All Contract Costs (Benefits & Fringe)
A contract initiator might find the proposal budget's contractual salaries pool is not inclusive of fringe costs such as unemployment contributions, social security, etc. With this in mind, a PI or their admin may need to factor 9% fringe into their contract. For example, a PI may submit a proposal with $10,000 total budgeted for their contract. The PI would need to divide $10,000 by 1.09 (to account for fringe). This would result in a total salary cost $9174.31 and associated fringe costs of $825.69.
12-month employees (release time)
12-month administrative employees (Chairs/Deans) cannot receive employment contracts for summer compensation from grants. However, they are able to submit for release time pending approval from their supervisor (when applicable) and the Office of the Provost. If this is necessary, please work with the Division of Academic Affairs for assistance with submitting release time requests.
fixed hourly rates: faculty summer contracts
We feel the need to elaborate on a point mentioned above in the Academic Affairs memo. For grant-funded contracts, the ORA office requires that faculty summer contracts utilize the maximum hourly rate calculated using the formula found on the AA memo. Please consider the following example: A faculty PI has project funds totaling $10,000 available in their 02 pool which is inclusive of all costs (salary & fringe). The PI's 9.5-month contract is $70,000 which, according to the formula, would put their hourly rate at $43.41 per hour. The $10,000 available would break down into $9,174.31 salary & $825.69 for fringe. At $43.41 per hour, the available budget would allow for a 211.34 hour contract. Contracts must be entered in whole hours so we suggest entering the contract for 211 hours. This will result in a contract with $9,159.51 salary and $824.35 fringe. The excess $16.14 remaining in the 02 contractual salaries pool after summer contract calculations may be allocated to another contract, potentially transferred to another budget pool, etc.

## Faculty Summer Contract Math
Faculty Summer Contracts: Practice Scenarios
Include example calculations
Below we have a few sample problems to help you succeed with your faculty summer contract calculations. If you need assistance with your faculty summer contracts, please speak with your school's Budget Officer or reach out to ask.ora@morgan.edu .
Complete the content above before moving on.
Knowledge check: Contract Math #1: Determining Hourly Rate A 9.5-month faculty PI earns $80,000 under their academic year contract. Their grant will fund the maximum allowable summer salary of 2.5 months and this PI will not receive any other compensation during the summer period. What would be the hourly rate to use on their grant-funded contracts for Summer 2026?
  - $49.62  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - Anything less than $49.62  [incorrect]
  Note on "$49.62": Great Job! ($80,000 * 26.3%)/(Total Summer Working Hours)
  Note on "Anything less than $49.62": No. For grant contracts the hourly rate should match the maximum hourly rate calculated using the Academic Affairs memo.
Knowledge check: Contract Math #2: Fitting Your Budget A faculty PI reaches out for help drafting their summer contract. According to their approved project budget, the total amount allocated to their contractual salaries Banner pool level is $19,000. With a 9.5-month salary of $70,000, what is the maximum summer salary amount that can be requested for the PI's contract without changing the budget?
  - $18,410  [incorrect]
  - $18,000  [incorrect]
  - $17,431  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - $17,500  [incorrect]
  Note on "$18,410": Incorrect. This amount is the maximum salary the PI can request among all projects for the summer. However, this amount does not factor in the 9% fringe benefits charged to faculty summer contracts. Including fringe this contract would cost $20,066; putting your budget in the negative.
  Note on "$18,000": Incorrect. Please try again.
  Note on "$17,431": Correct! While $18,410 is the total amount that may be requested in the summer for this PI, it does not factor in the budget ($19,000) or fringe benefit costs (9% on top of salary cost). $17,431 * 1.09 = $19,000.
  Note on "$17,500": Incorrect. Please try again.
Knowledge check: Contract Math #3: Balancing Multiple Projects & Periods A faculty PI has the following grants with funding available for Summer 2026 compensation: NSF Project: Budget: 2 months (salary & fringe) Performance Period: 9/1/25 - 8/30/26 NIH Project #1: Budget: .25 months (salary & fringe) Performance Period: 7/1/25 - 6/30/26 NIH Project #2: Budget: .25 months (salary & fringe) Performance Period: 7/31/26 - 6/30/27 With a 9.5-month salary of $93,176, what is the estimated salary cost for each contract? Also, what is the ideal order for the contracts to occur in the summer period?
  - NIH #1: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NIH #2: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NSF: (2/9.5) * $93,176 = $19,616 Contract Order: NIH #1, NSF, NIH #2  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - NIH #1: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NIH #2: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NSF: (2/9.5) * $93,176 = $19,616 Contract Order: NIH #1, NIH #2, NSF  [incorrect]
  - NIH #1: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NIH #2: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NSF: (2/9.5) * $93,176 = $19,616 Contract Order: NSF, NIH #1, NIH #2  [incorrect]
  Note on "NIH #1: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NIH #2: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NSF: (2/9.5) * $93,176 = $19,616 Contract Order: NIH #1, NSF, NIH #2": Great job! You need to consider the performance periods of each grant funding summer contacts. In order for costs to be allocable to a project they must occur during the performance period to which they are charged.
  Note on "NIH #1: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NIH #2: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NSF: (2/9.5) * $93,176 = $19,616 Contract Order: NIH #1, NIH #2, NSF": Incorrect. Please consider that contracts must occur within the performance period of the project.
  Note on "NIH #1: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NIH #2: (.25/9.5)* $93,176 = $2,452 NSF: (2/9.5) * $93,176 = $19,616 Contract Order: NSF, NIH #1, NIH #2": Incorrect. Please consider that contracts must occur within the performance period of the project.

## Special Compensation
What is Special Compensation?
https://articulateusercontent.com/assets/rise/assets/block-defaults/paraglide_thumb.jpg
Special Compensation is the mechanism by which a full-time regular employee may receive a one-time payment for work performed outside of their normal work duties. For example, a PI may choose to compensate a faculty member for participating in a training workshop. Grant-funded special compensation payments are limited to 5% or less of an individual's institutional base salary (IBS). For faculty this will be their 9.5-month academic contract. For staff & administrators this would be their 12-month employment contract. Special Compensation should be a rare occurrence.
How to Process a Special Compensation Payment
There is required training and an associated DocuSign form that must be completed for Special Compensation payments. To initiate this training, please contact Dr. Sophia Jacobs (sophia.jacobs@morgan.edu) in the Office of the Comptroller. The training must be completed before submitting the DocuSign form. The payment is processed via the Payroll department and will be received along with the individual's contracted salary paycheck. Special Compensation is charged against the 01 Banner budget pool level (Account: 01150) so be sure to verify there are sufficient funds.

## Processing Honoraria Requests
Ins and Outs: Honoraria Processing
In the world of grants, honoraria refers to one-time payments made to individuals for services rendered that are not based on a contractual agreement or an employer-employee relationship. Honoraria are often provided as a token of appreciation or recognition for an individual's participation in conferences, workshops, seminars, or other events sponsored by federal grant-funded projects or organizations.

## Timesheet Processing
Submitting Timesheets @ MSU
How to Submit a Timesheet
Here we will detail how to complete timesheets in Employee Self-Service.
Note To Faculty (Summer Contracts)
Faculty summer contracts require the faculty member to submit biweekly timesheets for approval by their supervisor. Please be sure to monitor your emails for OHR Announcements that will detail the timesheet submission date/time deadlines.
Go to Employee Self-Service (Timesheet)
First, to enter hours on a timesheet you must make your way to the Employee Self-Service portal of Banner where you will be prompted to enter your MSU credentials. You can find the Banner Links homepage here .
Access Your Available Timesheets
On the Employee Dashboard landing page you can find the "My Activities" section under which a button is labeled "Enter Time." Clicking on that will open a page with all available timesheets for all current contracts. You will need to enter time for each project on separate timesheets to ensure costs are properly allocated to the correct project budget. When you have identified the correct timesheet click on "Start Timesheet."
Enter Time
Each timesheet will be for a specific pay period as noted by the dates in the top left of the timesheet screen. The submission/approval deadline will also be noted in the top right of this screen. The employee will need to enter hours for each day worked. Once time is entered the employee will click on "Preview" button. On the next page if everything looks correct the employee will click the "Submit" button in the bottom right corner of the screen. Commonly used "Earn Codes": Regular Earnings: standard for hours worked Annual Leave Pay: utilized if you have banked annual leave Sick Pay: utilized if you have banked sick leave Holiday Pay: utilized for holidays such as Christmas, Memorial Day, etc. Some employees may not qualify for holiday pay based on their hire date and employment status. University Holiday Pay: An example for this would be the additional days of MSU's winter break outside of Christmas, Christmas Eve, and New Years Day.
Late Timesheets & Electronic Access Issues
There may be times when an employee misses the submission deadline or is unable to access their timesheet in Employee Self-Service. If a timesheet must be submitted late please use the DocuSign link here . Please be sure to include the grant budget's index and fund on the timesheet to ensure the salary costs are charged to the appropriate project. If an employee cannot access their timesheet in Employee Self-Service please contact the OHR HRIS team (hris@morgan.edu) for troubleshooting assistance. The DocuSign form linked above can be used until the technical issue is resolved.
Approving Timesheets @ MSU
How to Approve a Timesheet
Here we will detail how to approve a timesheet in Employee Self-Service.
First, to approve a timesheet you must make your way to the Employee Self-Service portal of Banner. You will be prompted to enter your MSU credentials. You can find the Banner Links homepage here .
Go to the "Approve Time" Page
On the Employee Dashboard landing page you can find the "My Activities" section under which is a link labeled "Approve Time." Click the link to load all timesheets pending your approval.
Time Entry Approvals
Above is the Time Entry Approvals page. Here, you can see all timesheets waiting for your approval. When you have identified the correct timesheet click on the employee's name.
Approve/Return Timesheet
It is the supervisor's responsibility to review the reported hours and ensure that they reflect the hours stated in the employee's contract. If the timesheet is correct you can select "Approve" in the bottom right. If a correction must be made please click the "Return for Correction" button to send the timesheet back to the employee.
Useful Information
Please note that typically a PI will be the timesheet approver for employees under their project(s) and the PIs timesheets would be approved by their immediate supervisor (Chair, Dean, etc). Additionally, OHR will send out reminder emails when timesheets are due for processing. It is important for a PI to watch for these emails. The timesheet submission deadlines may change due to holidays or university closure.
